T: You were only supposed to blow the doors off. Not the oven.
D: A crew of British crooks plan to steal a fortune in gold from the streets of Turin.
P: Serve the mains when the three little cars start the getaway through Turin.
S: Anchovies, lots of garlic and butter melted slowly into olive oil, kept warm over a flame, with raw fennel, capsicum, radish and bread for dipping.
Blow the bloody doors off cheese toasts
the gold bullion they're after, easy on the dynamite

Bread cut into neat bars, topped with grated aged cheddar and parmesan mixed with mustard and egg, grilled until golden. Mix 150g grated vintage cheddar, 30g parmesan, 1 tsp English mustard and 1 egg. Cut 6 slices of bread into neat bars and toast one side. Spread the cheese mix on the other side and grill until golden and bubbling.
Mr Bridger's cucumber and egg tea fingers
the crime boss running everything from his prison cell

Crustless fingers of buttered white bread with cucumber and mint cream cheese, and curried egg and cress, stacked on a plate like a proper English tea. Boil 4 eggs for 10 minutes, peel and mash with 3 tbsp mayo, a pinch of curry powder and salt. Beat 150g cream cheese with chopped mint. Butter 12 slices white bread. Spread 3 with cream cheese and top with thin cucumber slices, spread 3 with egg and cress, then close all six. Cut off the crusts and cut each into 3 fingers.
M: Veal or pork loin poached gently, chilled, sliced thin, covered in a sauce of tuna, anchovy, capers, mayo and lemon.
Turin beef agnolotti with brown butter
handmade pasta from Piedmont, the region of the job

Little pinched pasta pockets of braised beef and parmesan, tossed in nutty brown butter with crispy sage and more parmesan. Mix 300g shredded braised beef or cooked beef mince with 40g parmesan, 1 egg and nutmeg. Roll 400g fresh lasagne sheets thinner and cut into 6cm wide strips. Dot teaspoons of filling along each strip, fold over and pinch between each mound, then cut into pockets. Boil for 3 minutes. Melt 100g butter until nut brown with 12 sage leaves, toss the pasta through and finish with parmesan.
W: a Piedmont pudding from around Turin

Sugar cooked to a dark caramel and poured into a loaf tin, a custard of eggs, milk, cocoa, crushed amaretti and a splash of rum poured over, baked in a water bath at 160C for 45 minutes, chilled and turned out.
K: Hang on a minute, lads bicerin
a Turin café, and a great idea

The Turin café classic: thick hot chocolate, a shot of espresso and lightly whipped cream layered in a small glass. Heat 300ml milk and whisk in 100g chopped dark chocolate and 1 tbsp sugar until thick and smooth. Brew 4 espressos. Lightly whip 150ml cream. Pour the hot chocolate into four small heatproof glasses, gently pour an espresso over the back of a spoon on top, then float the cream. Serve straight away without stirring.

s.how: Melt 60g butter in 150ml olive oil over very low heat with 8 crushed garlic cloves and 1 tin anchovies until the anchovies dissolve. Keep warm over a candle. Dip sliced fennel, red capsicum, radishes and bread.

s.n: Blow the bloody doors off cheese toasts
s.note: the gold bullion they're after, easy on the dynamite
s.how: Mix 150g grated vintage cheddar, 30g parmesan, 1 tsp English mustard and 1 egg. Cut 6 slices of bread into neat bars and toast one side. Spread the cheese mix on the other side and grill until golden and bubbling.

m.how: Poach an 800g pork loin gently in salted water for 45 minutes until 63C inside, then chill. Blitz a 185g tin of tuna, 3 anchovies, 1 tbsp capers, 150g mayo and lemon juice until smooth. Slice the pork thin and cover with the sauce and more capers.

w.note: a Piedmont pudding from around Turin
w.how: Cook 150g sugar to a dark caramel and pour into a loaf tin. Whisk 4 eggs, 100g sugar, 500ml milk, 2 tbsp cocoa, 80g crushed amaretti and 2 tbsp dark rum. Pour over and bake in a water bath at 160C for 45 minutes. Chill and turn out.
